column1: # INFRA-123 — hazardous spellings that only mean something IN A LANGUAGE, and the language they mean
# it in.
# Read by BOTH enforcers: `.claude/hooks/bulk-edit-guard.sh` (the command, before it runs) and
# `scripts/harness/scan-symlink-following-enumeration.mjs` (the committed script).
# WHY THESE NEED A LANGUAGE AND THE OTHER TABLE DOES NOT. `find -L` is a command and a flag: the
# shell grammar is enough to attribute it, which is what `symlink-following-hazards.tsv` does. An
# IMPORT is different. `from glob import glob; glob(...)` is the symlink-following enumerator wearing
# an import the call site does not spell, and the identical text in JavaScript
# (`import glob from 'glob'`) is a package this repository depends on that does NOT follow. Reporting
# both is refusing the safe sibling; reporting neither is the rule the follow-up to PR #1886 withdrew
# rather than ship unenforced.
# So the subject is the PAYLOAD, and the reader for it is `hook_interpreter_payloads` in
# `.claude/hooks/lib/command-scan.sh`. `language` is matched against the interpreter that owns the
# payload, mapped through `scripts/harness/script-language.mjs` (INFRA-115) — so `python3`,
# `python3.12` and a `#!/usr/bin/env python` heredoc are one language, named once.
# COLUMNS, tab-separated:
#   id         the name this hazard is REPORTED under
#   language   the language row from `script-language.mjs` whose payloads this applies to
#   pattern    an ERE, matched against the payload TEXT
#   remedy     the safe sibling, stated at the finding
